AC-0422 — the hard horizon line at altitude: results

What the previous run didNothing verifiable. The prior run of this ticket wrote a single 5-line journal entry to tasks/AC-0422/continuity.md (fresh run, checklist read, the coordinator’s first hypothesis recorded) and then stopped at the token limit: no plan, no captures, no code, no gates (verified against git status and file mtimes). This run is a fresh derivation, not a write-up of lost findings.
The user’s frame, beforeseed 44, noon (T=0.5), shipped defaults (render 50 / fog 87 → the fog wall at 706.56 m), AWECRAFT_CAM=planet aimed at the local horizon from 800 m (radial altitude 941 m, the sky’s A-window blend w = 0.80). The new aim is env-gated (AWECRAFT_CAM_HORIZON=1, additive on the existing planet preset, unset = byte-identical old behaviour — the AC-0417/AC-0419 aim precedent); the limb/nadir/zenith aims cannot produce this view: the limb is the tangent to the R disc, which sits below the local horizon at these altitudes.

1. What the edge turned out to be

The measurement (row-median luminance, 0–255, down the 720-row frame; tasks/AC-0422/measure.py — a 75°-vertical-fov pinhole model, one row = 0.25°):

Diagnosis — a boundary drawn, not computed. Two hard edges, one root cause. In sky_on() (the default u_sky_alt = 1 local-zenith path of godot/core/aero_sky_gradient.gdshader):

  1. The local horizon — the branch switch is a literal step(0.0, -hl): the above branch (the local-zenith gradient thinned to space by the A window w, plus the horizon haze band) meets the below branch (mix(space, u_air, 1-w)) with a discontinuity of 64.15/255 in a single pixel row. That is the straight line across the frame. It is the sky’s own branch boundary, keyed to the local radial (the sky is correctly not world-Y-aligned), drawn as a hard step.
  2. The satellite body’s rim — the body’s per-fragment 100%-fog rim is exactly u_air (the single-source air colour: the env fog’s light colour, the body’s u_air and the sky’s air term are one pushed value — the AC-0384-r8 seam contract). The sky just beyond the rim is the below branch, which equals u_air only at w = 0 (ground level). At any altitude where w > 0 the rim meets a darker sky: a second, smaller drawn edge (12.43/255 in the before frame).

Root cause (the coordinator’s hypothesis, confirmed in the frame): a sky term evaluated against a fixed state rather than the player’s local one. AC-0417/AC-0419 re-keyed the sky to the local zenith with the A window w = Aero.sky_space(alt_rad) and space-thinned the below-horizon branch with the same w — so at w > 0 the sky’s horizon value and its below-horizon fill drift away from the fog colour the world is still dissolving into. The seam was exact by construction at w = 0; it is a hard edge at altitude. The fourth instance of the “curved world treated as flat” class, in its fog/haze form: the world fades to u_air, the sky beyond is something else, and the two meet in a line. It survived the previous sky fixes because AC-0419’s acceptance views were the ground dome, the zenith (looking up) and the limb (looking at the tangent) — the user’s frame is the one view none of them covers: looking at the local horizon from altitude.

2. What was changed

One switch, default ON, three terms — all in sky_on(). Settings key "sky_horizon" (default true — the user asked for the edge removed, twice; the AC-0205/AC-0398 default rule: conservative only when the user has NOT asked). The shader default is 0.0 = the pre-AC-0422 path bit-for-bit (the AC-0401 short-circuit convention: a material that never sees the push keeps the old look). A/B rides the boot env AWECRAFT_SKYHORIZON=0|1 (AWECRAFT_RAMPS pattern).

TermOldNew (u_horizon = 1)Contract preserved
below branchmix(space, u_air, 1−w)u_air at every altitudethe AC-0384-r8 single-source seam restored for w > 0: the fog fades to u_air, the body’s rim is u_air, the sky under the horizon is u_air — one colour at the seam. The air is not space-thinned: the air does not become space, the view does (F3: a coverage gap reads as haze, not a hole — still true, now brightly).
above-branch thinningmix(w², w, u)mix(w², w, u) · uthe horizon is spared: weight 0 at hl = 0 (the grazing ray sweeps the longest air column and keeps its colour — the bright band at the horizon is the atmosphere seen edge-on), w at the zenith (u = 1 keeps the weight exactly w — the sky is still space at A when looking up, AC-0417).
branch switchstep(0, −hl) + discsmoothstep(0, 0.03, −hl) (~2°), OR’d with the inside-disc termabove the horizon the switch is 0 in both paths — the above branch’s only change there is the ·u thinning.

Files: godot/core/aero_sky_gradient.gdshader (the u_horizon uniform + the three terms in sky_on); godot/world/world.gd (boot env preload + the change-gated push, _ac0401_push block 2c + one state var); godot/autoload/settings.gd (the "sky_horizon" default, with the AC-0205 rationale); godot/scenes/harness.gd (the env-gated AWECRAFT_CAM_HORIZON=1 aim, additive); godot/HARNESS.md §2 (the aim, in the AWECRAFT_CAM row). No new arm, no harness_data.yaml row (the aim is an option on the existing planet cam — the AC-0419 zenith-aim precedent). Fenced files (main.gd, game.gd, drop.gd, debug.gd) untouched; no TASKS.yaml edit; no commits. ARCHITECTURE.md owes no change (no new subsystem, component or convention — one switch on the existing sky push seam).

4. Evidence the recent sky work still holds

Protected contract (recent sky work)Evidence
Day sky bright (AC-0419: ground dome median 0.0 → 85.6)Provably unchanged at ground level: at w = 0 every new factor evaluates to its old value (·mix(1, u, 0) = ·1, mix(old, u_air, 0) = old, mix(below_old, below_soft, 0) = below_old) — bit-identical, no re-shoot owed for the ground dome (a02 stands).
Local-zenith keying (AC-0417: the sky knows where the player is)The above-branch gradient is the same local-zenith expression, untouched; only the thinning weight gained the ·u factor. The 800 m frame varies continuously with the local zenith (bright band at the local horizon, darkening toward the local zenith), not with world Y.
Sky is space at A when looking up (AC-0417)Zenith 2141: median 0.79 = pure space (above).
Atmosphere wraps the world, no boundary surface (AC-0419 acceptance)Limbs 2141 (above): smooth glow, no edge; and at 800 m the world’s fog, the body’s rim and the sky below the horizon now share one colour at every seam (the 12.43 rim step → the continuous rim band).
Engine fog single source (AC-0384 r8)The fix makes the sky obey the contract at altitude instead of drifting from it: below-branch = u_air = env fog colour = body rim, all w. The 706.56 m fog wall at 800 m (before-h800) is no longer a visible wall — the world, the rim and the sky are one colour where they meet.

6. What was deliberately not done

  • No re-baselining of standing values — the fluids-census and player-start drifts are attributed (control-run + documented staleness), left for their owning tickets; the genhash row’s stale reference note is flagged here, not edited.
  • No ARCHITECTURE.md change — nothing structural moved (checked: one uniform, one push, one settings key).
  • No new harness arm — the horizon aim is an option on the existing planet preset (the AC-0419 precedent), so no harness_data.yaml row and no harness_doc.py --render re-render was owed; the hand-written §2 row documents it.
  • No re-shoot of the ground dome (a02) — provably bit-identical at w = 0 (every new factor evaluates to its old value); a re-shoot would measure the switch, which the md5 below already proves.
  • No TASKS.yaml edit, no commits, no pushes — the fence holds; closeout is the coordinator’s.
  • No change to the star field, sun disc, limb term, haze band, or the sky_off path — the OFF path (u_horizon = 0) is the pre-AC-0422 shader verbatim.

7. The conservative fallback, proven

AWECRAFT_SKYHORIZON=0 re-shoot of the user’s exact frame (800 m, same seed/time/radius/drain): byte-identical to the before frame — md5 1c6107083534929c39c47bce63ba405a on both. The switch’s OFF path is not “close to” the old look; it is the old look.
